translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,
to the holy and faithful brothers in Christ Jesus who are in Colossae:
Grace to you and peace from God our Father.
For we have heard of your faith in Christ Jesus and of your love for all the saints,
because of the hope that is prepared for you in the heavens. You heard of this hope before, in the word of the truth of the gospel,
which has come to you. In all the world it is bearing fruit and growing, just as it is among you, from the day you heard and came to know the grace of God in truth,
as you learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,
and who also told us of your love in the Spirit.
For this reason we also, from the day we heard of it, have not ceased praying and asking for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding,
so that you may walk in a way worthy of God, pleasing him in everything, bearing fruit in every good work and growing in the knowledge of God,
strengthened with all power by the might of his glory, for all endurance and patience, with joy,
giving thanks to the Father, who has made us worthy of a share in the inheritance of the saints in the light,
who rescued us from the power of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of his beloved Son,
in whom we have redemption and the forgiveness of our sins.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

For by him all things were created in the heavens and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or lordships, or principalities and authorities. All things were created through him and for him.
He himself is before all things, and all things were established by him.
He is the head of the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that he himself may be first in all things;
for it pleased all the fullness to dwell in him,
and through him to reconcile all things to himself. Through him he made peace by the blood of his cross, whether on earth or in the heavens.
Once you were estranged and hostile in your minds because of evil deeds,
but now he has reconciled you by the body of his flesh and by death, so that he may present you holy, spotless and blameless before him,

if you continue in the faith, grounded and established, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel that you heard. This gospel has been proclaimed to all creation under heaven, and I, Paul, became its minister.
Now I rejoice in my sufferings for you, and in my flesh I complete what is lacking in the afflictions of Christ, for the sake of his body, which is the church,
of which I became a minister according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to fulfil the word of God,
the mystery that was hidden from the ages and from the generations, but has now been revealed to his saints,
to whom God willed to make known what is the wealth of the glory of that mystery among the Gentiles, which is Christ with you, the hope of glory,
whom we preach, teaching every person and instructing everyone in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect through Christ Jesus.
For this I labour and struggle according to his help, the help that he works in me by his power.
For I want you to know how great a struggle I have for you, and for the Laodiceans, and for those who have not seen my face in the flesh,
so that their hearts may be comforted and you may be joined together in love, toward all the wealth of fullness of heart and of understanding, to the knowledge of the mystery of God and the Father,
in whom all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
I say this so that no one may put you to shame with words of excess [?].
For though I am far away in the flesh, yet in spirit I am with you. I rejoice, because I see your good order and the firmness of your faith in Christ.
As you have learned through Christ Jesus, let us also walk in him,
rooted and built up and established on him by faith, as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
Take care that no one takes you captive by that love of wisdom and vain deception, by human teaching, by the order of this world, and not by what comes through Christ,
for in him all the fullness of the Godhead dwells bodily.
And you are filled in him,
in whom you were also circumcised with a circumcision not made with hands, by stripping off the body of your flesh, by the circumcision of Christ.
You were buried with him in baptism, and with him you also rose through faith, by the help of God, who raised him from the dead.
And you, who were dead through sin and the uncircumcision of your flesh, he made alive together with him, and he forgave us all our sins.
And for our sake he wiped out the handwritten record with its decrees, which was against us. He took it out of the way and nailed it to the cross.
He stripped the principalities and the powers, made them a public spectacle, and brought them to nothing in it.
Let no one judge you in matters of food and drink, or with regard to a feast, a new moon, or a sabbath,
which are an image of the things to come, but the body is Christ's.

Let no one get the better of you, if he wishes to, through humility and the worship of angels. He dwells on what he has not seen, pleasing himself [?], and is puffed up for no reason by the mind of his flesh,
and does not hold fast to the head, from which the whole body is formed and held together by joints and members, and grows with the growth that comes from God.
If you died with Christ to the ordinances of this world, why then, as though you were living in the world, do you lay down rules:
"Do not approach, do not even taste, do not even touch",
Which are all things meant to perish through their use, according to the commandments and teachings of men?
These are things that seem to have some word of wisdom, through self-willed endurance in that rule, and humility, and disregard for the body, but not in any honor for the satisfying of the flesh.
If you have risen with Christ, seek the things of heaven, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God.
Think on the things of heaven and not on the things of earth.
For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
When Christ, our life, appears, then you too will appear with him in glory.
Put to death those earthly members of yours: fornication, impurity, passions, evil desires, and covetousness, which is idolatry,
because of which the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience,
among whom you also once walked, when you lived in these things.
But now you too must put away all of these: wrath, anger, malice, blasphemy, and filthy talk from your mouth.
Do not lie to one another. Strip off the old man with his deeds
and put on the new man, who is renewed in knowledge according to the image of his Creator,
where there is neither Gentile nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision,
Put on, then, as God's chosen ones, holy and beloved: mercy, kindness, gentleness, humility, and long-suffering,
bearing with one another and forgiving yourselves, if anyone has a complaint against anyone. Just as the Lord forgave you, so you also forgive them.
And above all these put on love, which is the bond [literally: firmness] of perfection,
and let the peace of Christ be made firm in your hearts, the peace to which you were called [or: appointed] in one body; and be thankful.
And let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom. Teach and admonish yourselves with psalms, hymns, and songs; sing to God in your hearts with spiritual grace;
and whatever you do, in word or in deed, everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
Wives, submit to your husbands, as is pleasing to the Lord.
Husbands, love your wives and do not be bitter toward them.
Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing to the Lord.
Fathers, do not anger your children, so that they do not lose heart.
Slaves, obey your earthly masters in everything, not only before their eyes with eye-service as people-pleasers, but fear the Lord with sincerity [literally: simplicity] of heart.
And whatever you do, do it from the heart, as for the Lord and not as for people.
Know that you will receive from the Lord the reward of your inheritance. Serve the Lord Christ.
But whoever does wrong will be paid back for the wrong he did, and there is no partiality.
And you masters, give your slaves what is just and fair. Know that you too have a Lord in heaven.
Persevere in prayer, and keep watch in it with thanksgiving.
At the same time pray for us as well, that God may open for us a door for the word, so that we may speak the mysteries of Christ, for which I am in bonds,
so that I may make it known, as I ought to speak.
Conduct yourselves with wisdom toward those outside, and [?] the times.
Let your speech always be seasoned with grace, as with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.
Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful minister and our fellow servant in the Lord, will tell you everything about me.
I have sent him to you for this very purpose, so that he may learn how you are and comfort your hearts,
together with Onesimus, the faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. He will tell you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, greets you, and so does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas (you have received instructions about him; if he comes to you, welcome him),
and Jesus, who was called Justus. These are the only ones from among the circumcision who are my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ Jesus, greets you. He is always striving for you in his prayers, so that you may stand firm, perfect and glad of heart, in the will of God.
I bear witness for him that he has great love for you and for those in Laodicea and in Hierapolis.
Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, and so does Demas.
Give greetings to the brothers in Laodicea, and to Nympha and the congregation in her house.
And when this letter has been read among you, see to it that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn read the letter from Laodicea.
And say to Archippus: "Take care to fulfil the ministry you received in the Lord."
This greeting is in my own hand, Paul's. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.
